paragraphs: A cricket ball is the only piece of equipment in the sport that is deliberately allowed to change during play. The seam wears, one side is polished and the other is not, and the entire craft of fast bowling grows out of that asymmetry.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the balls as static pieces. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a second volume of the set is offered separately.
At $34 the set suits sports and equipment visualisation, broadcast graphics, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, game assets and editorial illustration. On sale since 2022.

A curved treadmill has no motor. The runner drives the belt with their own feet, the speed is set by where they stand on the curve, and it cannot be run on badly, which is exactly why gyms that care about form buy them.
The model is light at 24,519 polygons and 25,766 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification, and a rigged build is offered separately.
At $34 it suits gym and fitness visualisation, equipment marketing, e-commerce imagery, interior scenes, film sets and game environments. On sale since 2022.

A dehumidifier is a fridge that throws its cold away. Air is chilled past the dew point, water drops out into a tank, and the same air is warmed and returned, which is why a room with one running gets slightly warmer as it dries.
The model holds 127,362 polygons and 61,234 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in white. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 it suits appliance and interior visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, advertising, building services presentation, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Gold finishes on phones are a market signal rather than a material choice. The colour survives because in several of the largest markets it means something specific about status, and manufacturers who dropped it brought it back.
The model is light at 24,254 polygons and 12,890 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in gold, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen mockups, e-commerce and advertising imagery, interior and desk scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

The cone was invented at a fair when somebody ran out of dishes, and the format never went back. Every variation since, the wafer cup, the flat wafer, the rolled cone, is a different answer to the same problem of eating something cold without cutlery.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the wafers as static pieces. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $34 the set suits food and confectionery visualisation, packaging and menu imagery, advertising, cafe and retail scenes, film set dressing and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

Horn loading is the oldest way to make a speaker loud and still the most efficient. The flare matches the driver to the air, which is why a horn needs a fraction of the power a conventional box does and why the shape refuses to go away.
The model is very light at 13,856 polygons and 14,027 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, in red, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits audio equipment visualisation, e-commerce and retail imagery, interior and listening room scenes, advertising, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

The microwave is the only kitchen appliance whose interface has got worse over time. Everybody wants one dial and thirty seconds; the industry keeps adding menus, and a generic set is useful precisely because no particular one has to be defended.
This is a collection listing rather than a single object, supplying the ovens as static pieces in unbranded schemes. It carries CheckMate Lite and Pro certification.
At $34 the set suits kitchen and interior visualisation, appliance and e-commerce imagery, advertising, film sets, game environments and editorial illustration. On sale since 2015.

A geodesic dome encloses the most volume with the least material, which is why it was invented for radar stations and ended up on holiday. The triangles carry the load between themselves, so nothing inside needs a post.
The model is light at 67,650 polygons and 33,976 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits hospitality and tourism visualisation, landscape and campsite scenes, architectural presentation, advertising, film backgrounds and game environments. On sale since 2023.

A travel router exists to make one hotel login serve every device in the room. It sits between the guest and whatever the property is running, which is a privacy argument as much as a convenience one.
The model holds 34,470 polygons and 34,105 vertices in quads and tris with overlapping UVs, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits product and technology visualisation, e-commerce and packaging imagery, advertising, desk and travel scenes, film props and editorial illustration. On sale since 2026.

A pile of loose notes is a very specific image, and it is almost never how money is actually stored. Banded, counted and stacked is reality; heaped is fiction, which is why the heap is what illustration reaches for.
The model is light at 24,896 polygons and 12,552 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $34 it suits editorial and financial illustration, advertising and stock imagery, film and television props, game assets and interior scenes. On sale since 2024.

The placenta is the only organ a body builds and then discards, and it belongs to neither parent entirely. Everything about obstetric medicine that goes right or wrong in a pregnancy comes back to how well this structure attached and functioned.

The model is extremely light at 4,114 polygons and 4,115 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, supplied with the umbilical cord, so it runs in interactive material. It is built to CheckMate specification.
At $34 it suits obstetric and midwifery education, patient explanation, medical illustration, interactive learning and editorial work. On sale since 2025.

Phone colours are chosen years in advance and then become the thing people remember about a generation. The hardware differences between models are increasingly invisible, so the finish is doing most of the work of telling one year from another.
The model is light at 21,496 polygons and 11,423 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in green, and carries StemCell certification. Four further colourways are offered separately.
At $34 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen and interface mockups, e-commerce imagery, advertising, desk and lifestyle scenes, and editorial illustration. On sale since 2024.

Titanium was adopted for phone frames because it is stiffer for its weight than aluminium and takes a finish that does not look like paint. The colour names have become a category of their own, describing a surface rather than a pigment.
The model is extremely light at 8,356 polygons and 9,678 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in desert titanium, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen and interface mockups, e-commerce imagery, advertising, desk scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.

The largest phone in a range exists because a meaningful number of people use it instead of a tablet. Screen size is the only specification most buyers can judge in a shop, and the price ladder is built on that fact.
The model is extremely light at 8,582 polygons and 9,931 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, in desert titanium, and carries StemCell certification.
At $34 it suits product and technology visualisation, screen and interface mockups, e-commerce imagery, advertising, desk scenes and editorial illustration. On sale since 2025.
